title: Fix Publish Content UX: surface backend errors and refresh feeds on successful publish

requirements.summary: Show real backend error messages on Publish Content failures and keep the form usable for retries.
acceptanceCriteria: If publishing fails due to authorization (or any backend trap), the Publish Content page displays a user-visible error message derived from the thrown error (fallback to a generic message only if none is available).
The error message is displayed in English and is visible without requiring the user to open devtools.
The form remains usable after an error (user can correct and retry).

file_operations.description: Create a small utility to normalize unknown thrown values (including Internet Identity/agent errors and authorization Runtime.trap messages) into a user-facing English string with a safe fallback. Verify the authorization component's usage instructions before implementing.

Update publish failure handling to display the actual backend error message (when available) using the new error-message utility, rather than always showing a generic message. Ensure the error state does not lock the form (keep inputs enabled except while the mutation is pending) and clears appropriately on retry/edit. Verify the authorization component's usage instructions before implementing.

Update the publish mutation error handling to derive the toast message from the same normalized error-message utility so UI feedback is consistent with backend trap text when present. Verify the authorization component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Refresh article feeds after a successful publish and only show success UI after the publish mutation truly succeeds.
acceptanceCriteria: After a successful publish, navigating to Home and/or News shows the newly published article without requiring a hard refresh.
The “Published Successfully!” confirmation screen is only shown when the upload mutation succeeds (not on failed attempts).

file_operations.description: Ensure the upload success handler invalidates and refetches all article-feed related React Query caches (including keys that start with ['articles', ...] used by Home/News filters and search) so new submissions become visible immediately after publishing and subsequent navigation shows fresh data.

Adjust the publish flow to set the “Published Successfully!” state strictly after the upload mutation resolves successfully (and never on failure), and to avoid any UI state transitions that could imply success before the backend call completes (e.g., by relying on mutateAsync/await or equivalent success gating).
